incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx rate detected in prod edge (gateway). Error rate > 6% over 5m, paging oncall. Service: api-gateway.
Alice (oncall-sre): I'm on it, looking at the Grafana spike now.
Alice (oncall-sre): Observing a sharp increase in 502/504 from envoy upstreams 10.12.34.0/24  — looks like retries are amplifying failures.
Bob (eng-runtime): I see a surge in upstream 5xxs from backend-models pool, a lot of connection resets. Any recent routing changes?
Dan (ingress): I just deployed a route weight tweak to shift traffic for canary around 15:40UTC — changed route weights and adjusted retries on the virtualhost: retries: attempts: 3, per_try_timeout: 2s, host_selection_retry: true.
Alice (oncall-sre): Got config diff? Paste the envoy vhost snippet.
Dan (ingress): ```yaml
route:
  - match: /v1/generate
    route:
      cluster: models-v1
      retry_policy:
        retry_on: gateway-error,connect-failure,refused-stream
        num_retries: 3
        per_try_timeout: 2s
```
Priya (customer-success): Customers reporting increased latency and some request failures. We're getting a ticket from a large customer. Need ETA for mitigation.
Alice (oncall-sre): Hypothesis: retry policy + route weight change produced retry storms to a partially degraded models-v1 cluster, causing head-of-line 5xx amplification. First step: disable retries at the edge for /v1/generate and revert route weights.
Bob (eng-runtime): Agreed. If retries are over-forwarding to failing upstream, that will blow out connections. I'll prepare a quick rollback.
sre-bot: deploy-bot initiated rollback of envoy-route-config to rev 2024-11-07T15:30Z by Dan. (status: in_progress)
Alice (oncall-sre): Dan — can you remove retry_policy from that route or set num_retries: 0 and set per_try_timeout: 0s? I want no client-side retries for now.
Dan (ingress): Pushing change now to canary first, then global if green. Command: `kubectl apply -f envoy/vhosts/gateway-canary.yaml --namespace=ingress`
Dan (ingress): Canary went green — envoy canary shows 5xx down to 1.5% after disabling retries. Applying to prod now.
Alice (oncall-sre): Applying prod patch: `kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/envoy-gateway` and update configmap. Watch logs for 504s as connections drain.
Bob (eng-runtime): While that's rolling, I'm throttling upstream model cluster to reduce connection saturation: lowering max concurrent requests per worker and enabling circuit-breaker shadowing. Patch: set max_connections 1000 -> 300 on cluster config.
Priya (customer-success): Can we confirm which customers saw impact and send a quick heads-up? I'll draft a note.
Alice (oncall-sre): Quick customer impact: approx 4% of requests across the gateway window 15:36–15:48 UTC returned 502/504 intermittently; major customers A and C saw retries resulting in duplicate errors.
Dan (ingress): Prod config rolled. Monitoring shows 5xx at 0.9% and latency back to baseline.
Alice (oncall-sre): Good. Next steps: 1) keep retries off for /v1/generate until we investigate backend health, 2) add guardrails to not allow num_retries > 1 for that route in future, 3) run postmortem and include a checklist for canary route-weight changes.
Bob (eng-runtime): I'll open an RFC to adjust default retry policies and automatic circuit-breaker tuning based on upstream error rate. Also will add a k8s readiness probe audit to ensure bad pods were removed earlier.
Priya (customer-success): Sending interim status to impacted customers now: ETA for detailed postmortem by EOD.
sre-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Notify on-call rotation for handoff: @Bob now owns follow-up.
Alice (oncall-sre): Handover to Bob for follow-up and postmortem. I'll file the incident ticket with timeline and attach relevant logs.
Bob (eng-runtime): Acknowledged, taking ownership. Attaching quick debug commands we used: `kubectl logs -n ingress deploy/envoy-gateway -f --tail=200`, `curl -v -H "Host: api.example.com" "https://gateway/api/v1/generate"`, `istioctl proxy-config cluster envoy-gateway --name models-v1`.
Alice (oncall-sre): Thanks team. If anything regresses ping here. :thumbsup:"
